title: WebSocket / realtime
summary: WSS, Origin allowlist, socket auth, tokens in URLs, per-message authorization, and subscription IDOR.

checks.title: Authenticated sockets over WSS
checks.why: A ws:// socket carries a session or the page mixed-content-falls back to plaintext.
checks.validate: An authenticated message is observable on a plaintext WebSocket.

variants.name: ws:// upgrade
variants.payload:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
variants.expect: Must 4xx or redirect to wss. A 101 on port 80 is the finding if the socket is authenticated.
variants.why: A ws:// upgrade lets an on-path attacker read or tamper with the socket.

variants.name: Page socket URL
variants.payload: In DevTools, look at the page's new WebSocket(...) argument.
variants.expect: Must be wss:// on an HTTPS page. A ws:// URL is mixed content and often blocked — still record it.
variants.why: Reading the socket URL from the page shows whether it is wss and which host it targets.

checks.title: Origin allowlist
checks.why: The upgrade ignores Origin or reflects any origin, so a malicious page can open the victim's socket.
checks.validate: A handshake from https://evil.example is accepted on an authenticated socket.

variants.name: Arbitrary Origin
variants.payload:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Origin: https://evil.example
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: Must reject. A 101 is the finding if the cookie is enough to authorize.
variants.why: An accepted arbitrary Origin means the socket allows cross-site connections.

variants.name: null / subdomain
variants.payload:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Origin: null
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: null and https://evil.example.com.example must not match a substring allowlist.
variants.why: null and subdomain Origins test whether the allowlist is exact or substring.

checks.title: Socket authentication
checks.why: The socket is open to anyone, or the token is in the query string.
checks.validate: A message that should be authenticated succeeds without a current credential.

variants.name: No cookie / no token
variants.payload:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Origin: https://www.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
variants.expect: Must 401. If 101, send a privileged subscribe next — an open handshake plus authorized data is the finding.
variants.why: A 101 without any credential means the socket is unauthenticated.

variants.name: Token in the query string
variants.payload:
GET /chat?access_token=<token> HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
variants.expect: If it works, the token is now in logs and Referer. Prefer a header or a post-open auth message.
variants.why: A bearer in the socket URL leaks into logs and history.

groups.title: Messages and subscriptions
groups.summary: Every message is a request. Authorize it.

checks.title: Per-message authorization
checks.why: A member can send an admin action, or A can act as B, over an already-open socket.
checks.validate: A privileged or cross-account action executes.

variants.name: Cross-account send
variants.expect: A's socket must not deliver to B's inbox. Also try user_id, to, room.
variants.why: Sending as another user proves per-message authorization is absent.

variants.name: Admin action on member socket
variants.expect: Must be unauthorized. Confirm the side effect did not happen.
variants.why: A member invoking an admin action on the socket is a privilege gap.

checks.title: Subscription / channel IDOR
checks.why: SUBSCRIBE room:1002 returns B's events to A's socket.
checks.validate: An event about B arrives on A's connection.

variants.name: Subscribe to B's channel
variants.expect: Must refuse or stay silent. An order-updated event for B is the finding.
variants.why: Joining another user's channel is channel-level IDOR.

variants.name: Wildcard / broadcast
variants.expect: Wildcards must not expand past the caller's objects.
variants.why: A wildcard or broadcast subscribe can read every channel.

ws-origin.purpose: An accepted arbitrary Origin means the socket allows cross-site connections.
ws-origin.payload:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Origin: https://evil.example
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Cookie: session=<account-A>

ws-no-auth.purpose: A 101 without any credential means the socket is unauthenticated.
ws-no-auth.payload:
GET /chat HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Origin: https://www.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
